-- | Little-endian reads from a strict ByteString, and the builders the
--   writers use.
module Minify.Bytes
u8 :: ByteString -> Int -> Word8
u16 :: ByteString -> Int -> Word16
u32 :: ByteString -> Int -> Word32
u64 :: ByteString -> Int -> Word64
i32 :: ByteString -> Int -> Int32
i64 :: ByteString -> Int -> Int64
putU16 :: Word16 -> Builder
putU32 :: Word32 -> Builder
putU64 :: Word64 -> Builder
uleb :: Word64 -> Builder
sleb :: Int64 -> Builder

-- | Reads a ULEB128 at an offset: the value and the offset after it.

getSleb :: ByteString -> Int -> (Int64, Int)
cstringAt :: ByteString -> Int -> ByteString


-- | What the tool needs to know about an executable regardless of its file
--   format: its segments and sections, its symbols, where the loader fixes
--   pointers up, and which parts play which role in compaction. The Mach-O
--   and ELF readers each produce a <a>Loaded</a>.
module Minify.Format
data Format
MachOFormat :: Format
ElfFormat :: Format
data Arch
Arm64 :: Arch
X86_64 :: Arch

-- | A section's part in compaction: code, string literals, read-only
--   constants and static closures are compacted; anything else keeps its
--   bytes and addresses.
data Role
Code :: Role
Strings :: Role
Const :: Role
Data :: Role
Other :: Role
data SegRole

-- | the segment holding the code (and, in Mach-O, the file header)
SegText :: SegRole
SegData :: SegRole

-- | Mach-O's link-edit segment, rebuilt by the writer
SegLinkedit :: SegRole

-- | Mach-O's zero page: no file bytes
SegPageZero :: SegRole
SegOther :: SegRole
data Section
Section :: !ByteString -> !ByteString -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Bool -> !Role -> !Int -> !SectRaw -> Section
[secName] :: Section -> !ByteString

-- | the segment's name (Mach-O), or a synthetic one for an ELF program
--   header
[secSegName] :: Section -> !ByteString
[secAddr] :: Section -> !Word64
[secSize] :: Section -> !Word64
[secOffset] :: Section -> !Word64

-- | no bytes in the file (zero fill)
[secNoBits] :: Section -> !Bool
[secRole] :: Section -> !Role

-- | index in the format's own section list (Mach-O: n_sect - 1; ELF: the
--   header index)
[secOrig] :: Section -> !Int
[secRaw] :: Section -> !SectRaw

-- | The format-specific fields a writer has to reproduce.
data SectRaw
MachOSect :: !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> SectRaw
[msAlign] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[msRelOff] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[msNReloc] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[msFlags] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[msReserved1] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[msReserved2] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[msReserved3] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
ElfSect :: !Word32 -> !Word64 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> SectRaw
[esType] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[esFlags] :: SectRaw -> !Word64
[esLink] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[esInfo] :: SectRaw -> !Word32
[esAlign] :: SectRaw -> !Word64
[esEntSize] :: SectRaw -> !Word64

-- | A loadable region: a Mach-O segment or an ELF program header of type
--   PT_LOAD. Protections use the Mach-O encoding (1 read, 2 write, 4
--   execute).
data Segment
Segment :: !ByteString -> !SegRole -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> [Section] -> !Int -> Segment
[segName] :: Segment -> !ByteString
[segRole] :: Segment -> !SegRole
[segVmAddr] :: Segment -> !Word64
[segVmSize] :: Segment -> !Word64
[segFileOff] :: Segment -> !Word64
[segFileSize] :: Segment -> !Word64
[segMaxProt] :: Segment -> !Word32
[segInitProt] :: Segment -> !Word32
[segFlags] :: Segment -> !Word32
[segSections] :: Segment -> [Section]
[segOrig] :: Segment -> !Int
data Symbol
Symbol :: !ByteString -> !Word64 -> !Bool -> !SymClass -> !Int -> Symbol
[syName] :: Symbol -> !ByteString
[syValue] :: Symbol -> !Word64

-- | defined in a section of this file
[syDefined] :: Symbol -> !Bool
[syClass] :: Symbol -> !SymClass

-- | index in the format's symbol table
[syOrig] :: Symbol -> !Int

-- | How the carving treats a symbol.
data SymClass

-- | an external definition: begins a region, classified by its name
SymExternal :: SymClass

-- | a local definition the C compiler made: begins a fixed region
SymLocalC :: SymClass

-- | a local label GHC made (a return point, a local closure, a constructor
--   name string): a Haskell definition without a module of its own
SymLocalHs :: SymClass

-- | not a definition (a mapping symbol, a dead-strip marker)
SymIgnore :: SymClass

-- | What a reader produces. The raw format record stays with the reader's
--   module; <a>ldRaw</a> only says which one it is.
data Loaded
Loaded :: !Format -> !Arch -> Maybe [Word64] -> [(Word64, ByteString)] -> Maybe [Word64] -> !Word64 -> !Bool -> [Segment] -> [Section] -> [Symbol] -> Raw -> Loaded
[ldFormat] :: Loaded -> !Format
[ldArch] :: Loaded -> !Arch

-- | the file has an exact list of the pointer slots the loader fixes up
--   (Mach-O rebases, ELF relative relocations); when it does not, the
--   slots are found by parsing the static closures
[ldSlots] :: Loaded -> Maybe [Word64]

-- | slots the loader binds to a named symbol: (slot, symbol)
[ldBinds] :: Loaded -> [(Word64, ByteString)]

-- | when the link kept its relocations: the addresses of every 32-bit
--   absolute field in code, so that nothing else is taken for one
[ldAbsFields] :: Loaded -> Maybe [Word64]
[ldPageSize] :: Loaded -> !Word64
[ldPie] :: Loaded -> !Bool
[ldSegments] :: Loaded -> [Segment]

-- | in the format's own order
[ldSections] :: Loaded -> [Section]
[ldSymbols] :: Loaded -> [Symbol]
[ldRaw] :: Loaded -> Raw
data Raw
RawMachO :: Raw
RawElf :: Raw
isCompactedSection :: Section -> Bool
isCode :: Section -> Bool

-- | The suffixes GHC gives the symbols of a binding's parts.
hsKindSuffixes :: [ByteString]
hasHsKindSuffix :: ByteString -> Bool

-- | Whether a Mach-O local symbol's name is one GHC gives a local label on
--   Darwin: <tt>L</tt>, a unique of letters and digits, and a kind suffix
--   (<tt>_Lc4py_info</tt>, <tt>_Lg1Kz_closure</tt>). C's own local names
--   have words separated by underscores (<tt>_mark_closure</tt>) and no
--   <tt>L</tt>. ELF readers use the symbol's type instead: GHC's local
--   labels are untyped there.
ghcLocalLabel :: ByteString -> Bool

-- | Reading a 64-bit Mach-O executable: the header, the load commands, the
--   symbol table and the link-edit streams dyld reads (rebases, binds,
--   exports, function starts). Encoders for the streams the tool
--   regenerates live here too, next to their decoders.
module Minify.MachO
data MachO
MachO :: !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> !Word32 -> [LoadCommand] -> !ByteString -> MachO
[moCpuType] :: MachO -> !Word32

--   LC_CODE_SIGNATURE, ...)

data MSegment

-- | A pointer slot dyld slides: segment index, offset in the segment, type
--   (1 = pointer).

Rebase :: !Int -> !Word64 -> !Word8 -> Rebase

[rbOff] :: Rebase -> !Word64
[rbType] :: Rebase -> !Word8

--   segment (callers pass them sorted by offset).

data Bind
Bind :: !Int -> !Word64 -> !Word8 -> !Int -> !Word8 -> !ByteString -> !Int64 -> Bind
[bdSeg] :: Bind -> !Int

--   -3 weak lookup

-- | Decodes a bind or lazy-bind stream (DONE separates lazy records and
--   ends a regular stream; both are read to the end of the bytes).
decodeBinds :: ByteString -> [Bind]

-- | Encodes binds as an ordinary (non-lazy) stream, one full record each.
encodeBinds :: [Bind] -> Builder

-- | An exported symbol: name, flags, and the value (an offset from the
--   header for the ordinary kinds). Re-exports and stub-and-resolver
--   entries keep their extra data verbatim.
data Export
Export :: !ByteString -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> Maybe (Word64, ByteString) -> Export
[exName] :: Export -> !ByteString
[exFlags] :: Export -> !Word64
[exAddr] :: Export -> !Word64

-- | for a re-export: (ordinal, imported name); for stub-and-resolver:
--   resolver offset in exAddr2
[exOther] :: Export -> Maybe (Word64, ByteString)
decodeExports :: ByteString -> [Export]

-- | Builds the export trie. Node offsets are ULEB-encoded, so sizes are
--   iterated to a fixed point as ld64 does.
encodeExports :: [Export] -> Builder

-- | Function start addresses, given the __TEXT segment's address.
decodeFunctionStarts :: Word64 -> ByteString -> [Word64]
encodeFunctionStarts :: Word64 -> [Word64] -> Builder

-- | The kinds of reference the tool finds and rewrites. The first group is
--   AArch64 instruction forms, the second x86-64 forms and jump-table
--   entries, the third fields shared by every target: info table offsets
--   and pointer slots.
module Minify.Ref
data RefKind

-- | adrp + add pair (the pair's address; 8 bytes)
RAdrpAdd :: RefKind

-- | adrp + ldr pair for a GOT slot
RAdrpLdr :: RefKind
RB :: RefKind
RBl :: RefKind
RBcond :: RefKind
RCbz :: RefKind
RTbz :: RefKind

-- | a 4-byte signed displacement measured from an anchor stored with the
--   reference: x86 branches and calls, RIP-relative operands, and 32-bit
--   jump table entries (anchor: the table)
RRel32 :: RefKind

-- | an 8-byte signed displacement from an anchor: 64-bit jump table
--   entries
RRel64 :: RefKind

-- | a 4-byte absolute address, sign-extended (x86 in a non-PIE executable)
RAbs32 :: RefKind

-- | the SRT offset in the last 4 bytes of an info table
RSrt :: RefKind

-- | the con_desc offset of a constructor table
RConDesc :: RefKind
RLargeBitmap :: RefKind
RSlowApply :: RefKind
RFunBitmap :: RefKind

-- | an 8-byte absolute pointer in data
RPointer :: RefKind

-- | Bytes the field occupies.
fieldLen :: RefKind -> Int

-- | Whether the reference's anchor (the address the displacement is
--   measured from) is stored with it rather than implied by the kind.
anchored :: RefKind -> Bool
instance GHC.Internal.Enum.Bounded Minify.Ref.RefKind
instance GHC.Internal.Enum.Enum Minify.Ref.RefKind
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Minify.Ref.RefKind
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Minify.Ref.RefKind
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Ref.RefKind


-- | What an architecture's decoder needs from the analysis and reports
--   back to it, so that <a>Minify.Analysis</a> knows nothing about
--   instructions and the architecture modules know nothing about
--   definitions. One record is built per definition being decoded.
module Minify.Hooks
data Hooks
Hooks :: ByteString -> (Word64 -> Maybe Int) -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> String -> (Word64 -> Int -> IO Bool) -> (Word64 -> IO Bool) -> (Word64 -> Int -> IO ()) -> (Word64 -> RefKind -> Word64 -> Word64 -> IO ()) -> (Word64 -> Bool -> IO ()) -> (Word64 -> IO ()) -> (Word64 -> Int -> Bool -> IO ()) -> (Word64 -> IO Bool) -> (Word64 -> IO (Maybe Word64)) -> (String -> Word64 -> IO ()) -> (Word64 -> IO ()) -> (String -> IO ()) -> IO Bool -> (Word64 -> Bool) -> (Word64 -> Bool) -> (Word64 -> Bool) -> (Word64 -> Bool) -> !Bool -> (Word64 -> Bool) -> Hooks

-- | the whole file
[hkBytes] :: Hooks -> ByteString

-- | the file offset of an address, when the file backs it
[hkOffsetOf] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Maybe Int

-- | the definition whose code is decoded
[hkDefStart] :: Hooks -> !Word64
[hkDefEnd] :: Hooks -> !Word64
[hkDefName] :: Hooks -> String

-- | marks the bytes from an address as decoded; False when they were
--   already decoded or belong to an info table (decoding stops there)
[hkVisit] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Int -> IO Bool

-- | whether the bytes at an address belong to an info table
[hkIsTable] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO Bool

-- | marks bytes as data inside code (a jump table), never to be decoded
[hkMarkData] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Int -> IO ()

-- | a reference: field address, kind, target, anchor (for the anchored
--   kinds)
[hkRef] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> RefKind -> Word64 -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | a code label to decode from: address, whether an info table precedes
--   it
[hkLabel] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Bool -> IO ()

-- | an address in a data section that code refers to (a static closure, a
--   string, a jump table)
[hkData] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | a jump table: its address, entry size and whether entries are
--   displacements from it (else absolute addresses). Its entries are read
--   once decoding has settled, so that every table's address is known.
[hkJumpTable] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Int -> Bool -> IO ()

-- | whether an address lies inside an instruction already decoded (not at
--   its start): no jump table entry points there
[hkInterior] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO Bool

-- | the nearest jump table known to start after an address (tables of one
--   procedure are adjacent, and their entries look alike)
[hkNextTable] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO (Maybe Word64)

-- | an address fixed code refers to: what it lies in stays put
[hkPin] :: Hooks -> String -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | the 4 KB page an adrp names, when its uses cannot be followed
[hkPinPage] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO ()
[hkAnomaly] :: Hooks -> String -> IO ()

-- | the first pass only collects labels; its anomalies are not reported
[hkFirstPass] :: Hooks -> IO Bool
[hkInText] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Bool

-- | whether an info table ends at an address (a label with a table)
[hkHasTable] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Bool

-- | inside a definition that is Haskell code or data
[hkIsHaskellAt] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Bool

-- | inside a section the file backs
[hkInImage] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Bool

-- | the executable is position independent: no instruction carries an
--   absolute address
[hkPie] :: Hooks -> !Bool

-- | whether a 32-bit field at an address may hold an absolute address:
--   always, unless the link kept its relocations, which then decide
[hkAbsField] :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Bool
byteAt :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Word8

-- | Up to n bytes at an address (fewer at the end of the file's backing).
bytesAt :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Int -> ByteString
word32At :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Word32
word64At :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Word64


-- | AArch64: the instruction forms that carry a PC-relative or
--   page-relative address, decoded and re-encoded; the recursive-descent
--   decoding of a Haskell definition and the linear sweep of fixed code;
--   the stubs and islands the writer plants.
module Minify.Arm64

-- | What an instruction word is, as far as this tool cares.
data Insn

-- | destination register, page target
Adrp :: !Int -> !Word64 -> Insn

-- | target
Adr :: !Word64 -> Insn
B :: !Word64 -> Insn
Bl :: !Word64 -> Insn

-- | b.cond
BCond :: !Word64 -> Insn

-- | cbz / cbnz
Cbz :: !Word64 -> Insn

-- | tbz / tbnz
Tbz :: !Word64 -> Insn

-- | ldr (literal), ldrsw (literal), prfm (literal)
LdrLit :: !Word64 -> Insn

-- | br, ret: an unconditional transfer through a register
RegJump :: Insn

-- | permanently undefined, or a zero word: data, not code
Udf :: Insn
Other :: Insn
decode :: Word64 -> Word32 -> Insn

-- | Recursive-descent decoding from a label within a Haskell definition.
--   GHC's native code generator emits a closed set of address-carrying
--   forms: adrp+add (adjacent) for a label, adrp+ldr for a GOT slot, b for
--   jumps and tail calls, bl for foreign calls, and b.cond, cbz, tbz
--   within a procedure. Anything else that names an address is an anomaly.
decodeFrom :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | A linear sweep of fixed code for what it refers to. An adrp is paired
--   with its consumers when the register's uses can all be followed, and
--   each target pinned; otherwise the page is pinned. A target in code is
--   also a label: GHC code lies in fixed regions too (a module's unnamed
--   local closures follow whatever symbol precedes them, the C
--   <tt>main</tt> of the program's own module for one), and the info table
--   before such a label holds an SRT offset that must follow its closure.
--   
--   In a linker's erratum veneer (<tt>veneer</tt>), the target of a
--   <tt>b</tt> is a label even without a table. The linker moved one
--   instruction of a block into the veneer, put a <tt>b</tt> to the veneer
--   in its place, and the veneer's <tt>b</tt> returns to the rest of the
--   block. Decoding stops at the first <tt>b</tt>, so without this label
--   the rest of the block, and whatever only it reaches, would never be
--   decoded: its references would not be rewritten, and what they point at
--   could move or be removed while it stays put.
sweepFixed :: Bool -> Hooks -> Word64 -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | Whether a symbol names a linker's veneer for Cortex-A53 erratum
--   843419: bfd's <tt>e843419@...</tt> and lld's
--   <tt>__CortexA53843419_...</tt>.
isErratumVeneer :: ByteString -> Bool

-- | Re-encodes one instruction reference: the words at the field, its new
--   address, its new target, and the island for a branch that cannot
--   reach. Returns the new words, or an error.
patchInsn :: RefKind -> (Word64 -> Maybe Word64) -> [Word32] -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String [Word32]

-- | The instruction words with their address bits cleared, for comparing
--   code by shape.
maskInsn :: RefKind -> [Word32] -> [Word32]

-- | An abort stub at <tt>code</tt>: loads the message into x0 and calls
--   barf (or traps when there is no barf), then traps. 16 bytes.
stubCode :: Word64 -> Word64 -> Maybe Word64 -> Either String [Word32]

-- | A branch island at <tt>a</tt> for <tt>target</tt>: adrp x16; add x16;
--   br x16. x16 is the register the ABI reserves for exactly this.
islandCode :: Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String [Word32]
islandSize :: Word64

-- | A b or bl reaches this far either way.
branchRange :: Word64
needsIslands :: Bool

-- | <tt>add Xd, Xn, #imm12</tt> (64-bit, no shift) with the given Xn.
isAdd12For :: Int -> Word32 -> Bool

-- | <tt>ldr Xt, [Xn, #imm12*8]</tt> with the given Xn.
isLdr12For :: Int -> Word32 -> Bool
add12Imm :: Word32 -> Word64
ldr12Imm :: Word32 -> Word64

-- | Re-encodes an adrp at a new pc for a new target page.
encodeAdrp :: Word32 -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
encodeAdd12 :: Word32 -> Word64 -> Word32
encodeLdr12 :: Word32 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
encodeImm26 :: Word32 -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
encodeImm19 :: Word32 -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
encodeImm14 :: Word32 -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32

-- | Whether linear decoding stops after this instruction.
isBlockEnd :: Insn -> Bool

-- | The page offsets that the instructions following an <tt>adrp</tt> into
--   register <tt>rd</tt> add to it (C compilers may schedule the
--   <tt>add</tt> or <tt>ldr</tt> away from the <tt>adrp</tt>, and may use
--   one <tt>adrp</tt> for several accesses). Nothing when the register's
--   use cannot be followed: it is overwritten before any use, a branch
--   intervenes, or the window ends with it live.
adrpConsumers :: Int -> [Word32] -> Maybe [Word64]

-- | Fresh instructions for the abort stubs: <tt>adrp Xd, page</tt>,
--   <tt>add Xd, Xd, #lo</tt>, <tt>b target</tt>, <tt>bl target</tt>,
--   <tt>brk #0</tt>.
adrpInsn :: Int -> Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
addInsn :: Int -> Int -> Word64 -> Word32
bInsn :: Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
blInsn :: Word64 -> Word64 -> Either String Word32
brkInsn :: Word32
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Minify.Arm64.Insn
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Arm64.Insn


-- | x86-64: an instruction-length decoder that also says where an
--   instruction's address-carrying fields are, the recursive-descent
--   decoding of a Haskell definition (with GHC's jump tables), the linear
--   sweep of fixed code, and the abort stub.
--   
--   GHC's native code generator refers to addresses through rel32 branches
--   and calls, RIP-relative operands, and in a non-PIE executable through
--   sign-extended 32-bit immediates and displacements (the small code
--   model). Switches with dense cases compile to a jump table of
--   displacements from the table (64-bit, in the text section, on Darwin;
--   32-bit, in read-only data, on Linux with PIC) or of absolute addresses
--   (in read-only data, without PIC).
module Minify.X86
data X86Insn
X86Insn :: !Int -> !XKind -> Maybe (Int, Int) -> Maybe Int -> Maybe Int -> Maybe (Int, Int) -> !Word8 -> !Int -> Maybe (Int, Int, Int) -> Maybe (Int, Int, Int) -> !Bool -> X86Insn
[xLen] :: X86Insn -> !Int
[xKind] :: X86Insn -> !XKind

-- | a branch displacement: (offset in the instruction, 1 or 4 bytes), from
--   the instruction's end
[xRel] :: X86Insn -> Maybe (Int, Int)

-- | offset of a RIP-relative disp32, from the instruction's end
[xRip] :: X86Insn -> Maybe Int

-- | offset of a disp32 that is an absolute address (a SIB with no base)
[xAbs] :: X86Insn -> Maybe Int

-- | an immediate operand: (offset, size)
[xImm] :: X86Insn -> Maybe (Int, Int)

-- | the opcode byte, and its map (0: one byte, 1: 0F, 2: 0F38, 3: 0F3A)
[xOp] :: X86Insn -> !Word8
[xMap] :: X86Insn -> !Int

-- | (mod, reg, rm) with the REX bits applied
[xModRm] :: X86Insn -> Maybe (Int, Int, Int)

-- | (scale, index, base) with the REX bits applied
[xSib] :: X86Insn -> Maybe (Int, Int, Int)
[xRexW] :: X86Insn -> !Bool
data XKind
KJmp :: XKind
KJcc :: XKind
KCall :: XKind
KRet :: XKind

-- | jmp through a register or memory
KJmpInd :: XKind
KCallInd :: XKind

-- | ud2, hlt, int3: no fall-through
KTrap :: XKind
KOther :: XKind
KInvalid :: XKind

-- | Decodes the instruction at the start of the bytes (at least 15 should
--   be given when available).
decodeInsn :: ByteString -> X86Insn

-- | Recursive-descent decoding from a label within a Haskell definition.
--   GHC emits a switch's table lookup as one contiguous sequence, so a lea
--   of a table is recognised by looking at the instructions after it:
--   <tt>lea T(%rip), r; add (r, i, 8), r; jmp *r</tt> (64-bit
--   displacements, on Darwin) or <tt>lea T(%rip), r; movslq (r, i, 4), c;
--   add c, r; jmp *r</tt> (32-bit displacements, on Linux with PIC).
--   Without PIC the table holds absolute addresses and is read directly:
--   <tt>jmp *T(, i, 8)</tt>.
decodeFrom :: Hooks -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | Every jump table a definition's bytes name, found by scanning them for
--   the lookup idiom rather than by reaching the code: a table's entries
--   can only be read once the tables that follow it are known, and the
--   code that names a table may itself be reachable only through another
--   table. Returns (table address, entry size, relative).
scanTables :: Hooks -> [(Word64, Int, Bool)]

-- | Reads a jump table's entries, once decoding has settled: each is a
--   reference from the table to a block, and a label to decode from.
--   Entries are read while they are plausible: a displacement that is zero
--   (a missing case) or negative and lands in the definition, or an
--   absolute address in it; never past the next table, and never one that
--   lands inside an instruction already decoded, which only a misread
--   entry does.
tableEntries :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Int -> Bool -> IO ()

-- | A linear sweep of fixed code: every address it names inside a Haskell
--   definition is pinned. A byte that decodes as nothing is skipped.
sweepFixed :: Hooks -> Word64 -> Word64 -> IO ()

-- | An abort stub at <tt>code</tt>: lea rdi, [msg]; call barf; ud2. 16
--   bytes.
stubCode :: Word64 -> Word64 -> Maybe Word64 -> [Word8]
stubSize :: Word64

-- | rel32 reaches 2 GB either way: no islands are ever needed.
branchRange :: Word64
needsIslands :: Bool
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Minify.X86.XKind
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.X86.X86Insn
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.X86.XKind


-- | GHC's z-encoding of symbol names, and how a linked symbol's name
--   splits into package, module, binding and kind.
module Minify.ZEncoding

-- | Decodes a z-encoded string. Unknown escapes are left as they are.
zdecode :: String -> String

-- | A GHC-generated symbol, split: package (z-encoded, may be empty for
--   the main program), module (z-encoded), binding (z-encoded), kind
--   suffix.
data HsName
HsName :: !ByteString -> !ByteString -> !ByteString -> !ByteString -> HsName
[hsPackage] :: HsName -> !ByteString
[hsModule] :: HsName -> !ByteString
[hsBinding] :: HsName -> !ByteString
[hsKind] :: HsName -> !ByteString

-- | Splits a linked symbol name (with its leading underscore on Darwin,
--   without on ELF). A module component starts with an uppercase letter; a
--   binding and a module never contain an underscore, since z-encoding
--   escapes it, so the components are unambiguous.
parseHsName :: ByteString -> Maybe HsName

-- | <tt>package:Module.binding</tt>, or <tt>Module.binding</tt> for the
--   main program.
displayName :: HsName -> String

-- | The package name without its version and hash: <tt>unison-runtime</tt>
--   from <tt>unisonzmruntimezm0zi0zi0zmIhqCSoMNjyC4h5j74gBxPE</tt>.
packageBase :: ByteString -> String
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Minify.ZEncoding.HsName
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.ZEncoding.HsName


-- | Carving the file into definitions, finding every reference between
--   them, and deciding which ones are kept. See design.md.
module Minify.Analysis
data Kind
Haskell :: Kind
Fixed :: Kind

-- | A definition: the bytes from one symbol to the next, less the info
--   table that belongs to the next.
data Def
Def :: !Int -> !ByteString -> [ByteString] -> Maybe HsName -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Int -> !Kind -> !Int -> !Bool -> Def
[dIndex] :: Def -> !Int
[dName] :: Def -> !ByteString

-- | other symbols at the same address
[dAliases] :: Def -> [ByteString]
[dHs] :: Def -> Maybe HsName

-- | the symbol's address (the label; code starts here)
[dSym] :: Def -> !Word64

-- | first byte (the info table, when there is one)
[dStart] :: Def -> !Word64
[dEnd] :: Def -> !Word64

-- | index into <a>imSections</a>
[dSect] :: Def -> !Int
[dKind] :: Def -> !Kind
[dHead] :: Def -> !Int

-- | a local closure, static closure or string split off the definition
--   named by its symbol, or named by a local label
[dLocal] :: Def -> !Bool
data Image
Image :: Loaded -> !ByteString -> Vector Section -> Vector (Word64, Word64, Word64) -> Vector Def -> Vector Word64 -> [Symbol] -> Vector (Word64, Word64) -> [Segment] -> RawImage -> Image
[imLoaded] :: Image -> Loaded
[imBytes] :: Image -> !ByteString
[imSections] :: Image -> Vector Section

-- | (address, size, file offset) of sections with file contents, by
--   address
[imSectMap] :: Image -> Vector (Word64, Word64, Word64)
[imDefs] :: Image -> Vector Def
[imStarts] :: Image -> Vector Word64
[imSymbols] :: Image -> [Symbol]

-- | pointer slots as (slot address, value stored there), by address: the
--   loader's list when it has one, otherwise what the analysis found
[imSlots] :: Image -> Vector (Word64, Word64)
[imSegments] :: Image -> [Segment]
[imRaw] :: Image -> RawImage

-- | The format's own record, for the writer.
data RawImage
RawMachOImage :: MachO -> [Rebase] -> RawImage
RawElfImage :: Elf -> RawImage
data RefKind

-- | adrp + add pair (the pair's address; 8 bytes)
RAdrpAdd :: RefKind

-- | adrp + ldr pair for a GOT slot
RAdrpLdr :: RefKind
RB :: RefKind
RBl :: RefKind
RBcond :: RefKind
RCbz :: RefKind
RTbz :: RefKind

-- | a 4-byte signed displacement measured from an anchor stored with the
--   reference: x86 branches and calls, RIP-relative operands, and 32-bit
--   jump table entries (anchor: the table)
RRel32 :: RefKind

-- | an 8-byte signed displacement from an anchor: 64-bit jump table
--   entries
RRel64 :: RefKind

-- | a 4-byte absolute address, sign-extended (x86 in a non-PIE executable)
RAbs32 :: RefKind

-- | the SRT offset in the last 4 bytes of an info table
RSrt :: RefKind

-- | the con_desc offset of a constructor table
RConDesc :: RefKind
RLargeBitmap :: RefKind
RSlowApply :: RefKind
RFunBitmap :: RefKind

-- | an 8-byte absolute pointer in data
RPointer :: RefKind
data Analysis
Analysis :: Image -> Vector (Vector (Word64, Word8, Word64, Word64)) -> Vector Bool -> Vector Bool -> Vector Bool -> Vector Bool -> [String] -> Int -> Bool -> Map String Int -> Vector (Word64, Word8, Word64, Word64) -> Vector Int -> Map String Int -> [String] -> Analysis
[anImage] :: Analysis -> Image

-- | references, per definition index: (field address, kind, target,
--   anchor)
[anRefs] :: Analysis -> Vector (Vector (Word64, Word8, Word64, Word64))
[anPinned] :: Analysis -> Vector Bool
[anKept] :: Analysis -> Vector Bool
[anCut] :: Analysis -> Vector Bool

-- | cut definitions that a kept one still refers to
[anCutReferenced] :: Analysis -> Vector Bool
[anAnomalies] :: Analysis -> [String]
[anRoots] :: Analysis -> Int
[anKeepConDesc] :: Analysis -> Bool
[anPinCounts] :: Analysis -> Map String Int

-- | references from slots outside every definition: (slot, kind, target,
--   anchor)
[anLoose] :: Analysis -> Vector (Word64, Word8, Word64, Word64)

-- | the representative of each definition: itself, or the identical one it
--   is folded onto
[anRep] :: Analysis -> Vector Int

-- | things counted along the way, for the report
[anCounts] :: Analysis -> Map String Int
[anNotes] :: Analysis -> [String]
data Options
Options :: [String] -> Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> [RefKind] -> Maybe (Word64, Word64) -> Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> [(Word64, Word64)] -> [(Word64, Bool)] -> Bool -> [(Word64, Word64)] -> [Word64] -> [(Word64, Word64)] -> Options
[optRemovePrefixes] :: Options -> [String]
[optKeepDead] :: Options -> Bool

-- | keep constructor name strings (con_desc) reachable; otherwise they are
--   dropped and the fields point at one empty string
[optKeepConDesc] :: Options -> Bool

-- | which sections' definitions are split at internal closures and strings
--   (for debugging)
[optSplitText] :: Options -> Bool
[optSplitData] :: Options -> Bool
[optSplitStrings] :: Options -> Bool

-- | debugging: which reference kinds may split data, and an address range
--   the data splits are limited to
[optDataSplitKinds] :: Options -> [RefKind]
[optSplitRange] :: Options -> Maybe (Word64, Word64)

-- | debugging: rewrite pointer slots in fixed data (else pin their
--   targets); rewrite SRT fields in fixed code (else pin)
[optPatchFixedPointers] :: Options -> Bool
[optPatchFixedSrt] :: Options -> Bool

-- | fold identical code and strings onto one copy
[optFold] :: Options -> Bool

-- | debugging: only definitions starting in one of these ranges may be
--   folded (empty: all)
[optFoldRange] :: Options -> [(Word64, Word64)]

-- | code labels known from elsewhere (verify passes the planned entry of
--   every kept definition, since a label only a removed closure named
--   would otherwise go undecoded in the output): address, has a table
[optExtraLabels] :: Options -> [(Word64, Bool)]

-- | debugging: every GOT entry roots what it holds, instead of being an
--   edge from the code that loads it
[optGotRoots] :: Options -> Bool

-- | debugging: definitions starting in these ranges are kept whatever
--   reaches them
[optKeepRanges] :: Options -> [(Word64, Word64)]

-- | static closures known from elsewhere (verify passes every kept data
--   definition's place)
[optExtraData] :: Options -> [Word64]

-- | debugging: definitions starting in these ranges stay where they are
[optPinRanges] :: Options -> [(Word64, Word64)]
loadImage :: ByteString -> Either String Image
analyze :: Options -> Image -> IO Analysis

-- | The definition containing an address.
defAt :: Image -> Word64 -> Maybe Def

-- | The file offset of a virtual address, if it is backed by file bytes.
fileOffsetOf :: Image -> Word64 -> Maybe Word64
isCompactedSection :: Section -> Bool
isCode :: Section -> Bool
hsDisplay :: Def -> String
tableSize :: ByteString -> Int -> Int
imFormat :: Image -> Format
imArch :: Image -> Arch
imPie :: Image -> Bool
imPageSize :: Image -> Word64
imBinds :: Image -> [(Word64, ByteString)]
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Minify.Analysis.Kind
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Analysis.Def
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Analysis.Kind


-- | Where every kept definition goes, and how the segments are split so
--   the file omits the pages compaction frees. See design.md,
--   <a>Layout</a>.
module Minify.Layout
data Plan
Plan :: Vector Word64 -> Vector Word64 -> [Piece] -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> [(Word64, Word64)] -> [Piece] -> Map Word64 Word64 -> (Word64, Word64) -> (Word64, Word64) -> Map Int Stub -> !Word64 -> (Word64, Word64) -> Plan

-- | new start address of each definition (meaningful for kept ones)
[plNewStart] :: Plan -> Vector Word64

-- | where each placed definition's own bytes go (0 when not placed)
[plPlacedStart] :: Plan -> Vector Word64
[plPieces] :: Plan -> [Piece]

-- | file offset where the pieces end: the link-edit data (Mach-O) or the
--   section headers and symbol table (ELF) follow
[plLinkeditOff] :: Plan -> !Word64
[plLinkeditVm] :: Plan -> !Word64

-- | bytes the holes save
[plSaved] :: Plan -> !Word64
[plHoles] :: Plan -> [(Word64, Word64)]

-- | the pieces in load-command order (the segment numbering the loader
--   sees)
[plOrder] :: Plan -> [Piece]

-- | branch islands: target address to island address
[plIslands] :: Plan -> Map Word64 Word64

-- | the patch area in the code section (islands, abort stubs, their
--   messages, ELF program headers): address and size
[plIslandPool] :: Plan -> (Word64, Word64)

-- | the patch area in data (closure stubs): address and size
[plDataArea] :: Plan -> (Word64, Word64)

-- | abort stubs for cut definitions still referred to, by definition index
[plStubs] :: Plan -> Map Int Stub

-- | the empty string constructor names point at when they are dropped (0
--   when kept)
[plEmptyString] :: Plan -> !Word64

-- | where an ELF output's program headers go: address and the bytes
--   reserved
[plPhdrArea] :: Plan -> (Word64, Word64)

-- | A segment of the output: a run of the original segment's address space
--   that the file keeps, with its clipped sections.
data Piece
Piece :: ByteString -> Segment -> !Bool -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Word64 -> [Section] -> Piece
[pcName] :: Piece -> ByteString

-- | the segment it was cut from
[pcSegment] :: Piece -> Segment

-- | not the first piece of its segment
[pcExtra] :: Piece -> !Bool
[pcVmStart] :: Piece -> !Word64

-- | end of the address range the piece covers
[pcVmEnd] :: Piece -> !Word64

-- | end of the file-backed part (the rest is zero fill)
[pcFileEnd] :: Piece -> !Word64
[pcFileOff] :: Piece -> !Word64
[pcSections] :: Piece -> [Section]

-- | A replacement for a cut definition that is still referred to.
data Stub
Stub :: !Word64 -> !Word64 -> !Int -> !Word64 -> ByteString -> Maybe Word64 -> Stub

-- | the code label (its info table precedes it)
[sbCode] :: Stub -> !Word64

-- | start of the info table
[sbTable] :: Stub -> !Word64
[sbTableSize] :: Stub -> !Int

-- | the message string
[sbMsg] :: Stub -> !Word64
[sbMsgText] :: Stub -> ByteString

-- | the static closure, for a cut data definition
[sbClosure] :: Stub -> Maybe Word64

-- | The second argument caps the number of holes (segments added); the
--   third puts the extra code-segment pieces after the data pieces in the
--   load commands, so that the data segments keep indices dyld's opcodes
--   can express however many holes the code segment has (Mach-O only).
--   <tt>packRoles</tt> names the sections whose movable definitions are
--   packed first-fit; the rest keep their order (a debugging knob).
plan :: Analysis -> Int -> Bool -> [Role] -> Maybe (Word64, Word64) -> Bool -> Maybe (Word64, Word64) -> Either String Plan

-- | The new address of an old one: moved with its definition, or unchanged
--   when it lies in nothing that moves. Nothing for an address inside a
--   definition that is not kept.
newAddrOf :: Analysis -> Plan -> Word64 -> Maybe Word64

-- | The file offset of a new address in the output.
newFileOffsetOf :: Plan -> Word64 -> Maybe Word64

-- | The abort stub's code, on either architecture.
stubCodeSize :: Word64
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Layout.Piece
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Layout.Stub


-- | Checking the output by analyzing it the same way as the input: every
--   kept definition must have the same references, each landing where the
--   plan says its old target went. See design.md, "Checking the result".
module Minify.Verify

-- | Problems found, as messages; empty when the output checks out.
verify :: Analysis -> Plan -> ByteString -> IO [String]


-- | What the writers share: the choices made on the command line, the
--   statistics they report, and the relocation of an address through the
--   plan (including to the stub of a cut definition).
module Minify.Relocate

-- | The flag keeps Haskell definitions in the export trie; by default only
--   the other symbols stay exported, since nothing looks a Haskell closure
--   up by name with dlsym. <a>rwStrip</a> drops the symbol table (all but
--   the undefined symbols the stubs bind through) and the function starts.
data Choices
Choices :: Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> Choices
[rwKeepHaskellExports] :: Choices -> Bool
[rwStrip] :: Choices -> Bool
[rwZeroFolded] :: Choices -> Bool
data Stats
Stats :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Stats
[stSymbolsKept] :: Stats -> Int
[stSymbolsDropped] :: Stats -> Int
[stRebases] :: Stats -> Int
[stBinds] :: Stats -> Int
[stExports] :: Stats -> Int
[stLinkeditBytes] :: Stats -> Int
[stFileBytes] :: Stats -> Int

-- | The new address of an old one, or the stub that replaces a cut
--   definition it points into; an error for a removed one.
relocate :: Analysis -> Plan -> Word64 -> Either String Word64
alignUp :: Word64 -> Word64 -> Word64
toStrict :: Builder -> ByteString
hex :: Word64 -> String

-- | The address of a defined symbol, by name.
definedSymbol :: Image -> ByteString -> Maybe Word64
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Minify.Relocate.Stats


-- | Finishing a Mach-O output: the symbol table, the dyld streams
--   (rebases, binds, exports), the function starts, and the load commands
--   that describe the pieces. See design.md, "Layout and rewriting".
module Minify.MachOWrite

-- | The link-edit data to append after the pieces, the action that writes
--   the header and load commands, and the statistics.
parts :: Analysis -> Plan -> Choices -> MachO -> [Rebase] -> IO (ByteString, Ptr Word8 -> IO (), Stats)


-- | Finishing an ELF output: the program headers (in the patch area, since
--   the holes add some and the original table has no room), the section
--   headers with the compacted sections cut into pieces, the symbol table
--   relocated, and the dynamic symbols and relative relocations patched in
--   place. See design.md, <a>ELF</a>.
module Minify.ElfWrite

-- | The bytes to append after the pieces (non-loaded sections, the symbol
--   table, the section headers), the action that writes the ELF header,
--   the program headers and the in-place fixes, and the statistics.
parts :: Analysis -> Plan -> Choices -> Elf -> IO (ByteString, Ptr Word8 -> IO (), Stats)


-- | Producing the output file: copying and relocating the kept definitions
--   into the planned layout, then handing the format's writer the file to
--   finish (headers, link-edit data, symbol tables). See design.md,
--   "Layout and rewriting".
module Minify.Rewrite
rewrite :: Analysis -> Plan -> Choices -> IO (ByteString, Stats)
data Stats
Stats :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Stats
[stSymbolsKept] :: Stats -> Int
[stSymbolsDropped] :: Stats -> Int
[stRebases] :: Stats -> Int
[stBinds] :: Stats -> Int
[stExports] :: Stats -> Int
[stLinkeditBytes] :: Stats -> Int
[stFileBytes] :: Stats -> Int

-- | The flag keeps Haskell definitions in the export trie; by default only
--   the other symbols stay exported, since nothing looks a Haskell closure
--   up by name with dlsym. <a>rwStrip</a> drops the symbol table (all but
--   the undefined symbols the stubs bind through) and the function starts.
data Choices
Choices :: Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> Choices
[rwKeepHaskellExports] :: Choices -> Bool
[rwStrip] :: Choices -> Bool
